prompt: Inserting 100,000 rows one at a time takes 10 minutes, mostly in per-statement overhead.
why: Batch 1,000 rows per statement and pay the fixed cost 100 times instead of 100,000.
trap: Faster hardware doesn't remove fixed per-call costs.

prompt: Appending to a dynamic array occasionally copies everything into a new block, yet appends are still called O(1).
why: Doubling capacity spreads each copy across many cheap appends: O(1) amortized.
trap: One expensive operation doesn't make the average expensive.

prompt: A logger sends each log line as its own network packet, and the overhead uses more bandwidth than the logs themselves.
tells: each log line as its own network packet
why: Buffer lines and flush in batches so headers are shared across many lines.
trap: Batching adds a little delay; usually a fine trade.

prompt: A client opens a new HTTPS connection for every API call, paying a TLS handshake each time.
tells: new HTTPS connection for every API call
why: Reuse connections (keep-alive) so one handshake covers many calls.
trap: Latency numbers explain the cost; reuse is how you spread it.
